summary_rationale: MCX operates a near-monopoly (>98%–99% domestic market share) in Indian non-agricultural commodity derivatives across bullion, energy, and base metals, reinforced by the central counterparty network effects of MCXCCL and a Core Settlement Guarantee Fund that reached ₹1,472.16 crore as of September 30, 2026. Following the October 2023 migration from 63 Moons to the TCS Commodity Derivatives Platform, FY26 operating revenue doubled to ₹2,302 crore with 71% operating margins, 71.4% ROCE, and ₹3,035 crore in operating cash flow, followed by Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹800 crore and 76% operating margins as options notional ADT scaled to ₹12.00 lakh crore, options premium ADT reached ₹10,291 crore, and H1 FY27 traded clients hit 19.8 lakh (14.98 lakh in Q2). It earns COMPOUNDER_PASS for its asset-light toll-booth economics, structural domestic hedging expansion (electricity futures at ~75% share, Nov 2026 base-metal delivery hub consolidation), and zero-debt fortress balance sheet, paired with PASS_WITH_WATCH on KPIs due to: (1) recurring IT opex stepping up for 2x processing capacity alongside volume-linked CME energy license fees (~10% of energy revenue), (2) a ~25% normalized effective tax rate (after Q2's 28.9% MCXCCL catch-up) and the temporary nature of Q2's zero SGF contribution holiday, (3) bullion/energy concentration (~97.6% of ADT), (4) compressed 15% FY26 dividend payout as reserves accumulate, and (5) regulatory/operational governance scrutiny (Oct 2025 UCC outage, May 2025 ₹25 lakh SEBI disclosure penalty, and ongoing data-centre relocation review).
